config.title: Gardens of the World Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Getting to the Gärten der Welt in Marzahn, opening times, the cable car, tickets and what to see first.

items.q: How do I get to the Gardens of the World in Berlin?
items.a: Take the **U5 from Alexanderplatz towards Hönow to Kienberg (Gärten der Welt)**, about 26 minutes. From there the cable car runs over the Kienberg to the main entrance. When it is not running, walk about 15 minutes through the Kienbergpark or take the X69 bus to Blumberger Damm/Gärten der Welt.

items.q: What are the opening hours of the Gärten der Welt?
items.a: The park opens daily at **09:00**, the Japanese Garden at 10:00. Ticket desks and gates close at **18:00 in October and March, 16:00 from November to February and 20:00 from April to September**, and the themed gardens stay open until then.

items.q: When does the Gärten der Welt cable car run?
items.a: **Daily from 10:00 to 17:00 until 1 November 2026.** From 2 November it stops for its annual overhaul. From 5 December it runs on Saturdays and Sundays from 10:00 to 16:30, daily over the Christmas holidays except 24 and 31 December, and daily from 30 January to 7 February.

items.q: How much does a ticket cost?
items.a: An adult day ticket costs **EUR 9 until 31 October and EUR 4 from 1 November.** The combination ticket with a return cable car ride costs EUR 12.90 in summer and EUR 6.90 in winter. Children up to 5 go free.

items.q: Are all the gardens open in winter?
items.a: No. In past winters the **Japanese and Korean gardens and the Lebanon garden cabinet** closed from early November until the end of March. The Chinese Garden, the Oriental garden and the indoor Balinese Garden are the core of a winter visit.

items.q: How long do I need at the Gardens of the World?
items.a: **Three to four hours** to see all 13 gardens at an easy pace. With two hours, I would see the Chinese, Japanese, Balinese, Oriental and Korean gardens, in that order of importance.

items.q: Is the Gardens of the World worth it on a short trip to Berlin?
items.a: On a two-day first visit, usually not, because the round trip and a proper look take most of half a day. From the third day on, it is one of the best half days in Berlin, especially for garden lovers and families.
